title: Introduce CI Stitcher and dependency refinery to consolidate presubmit and release hooks
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Consolidates presubmit and release automation hooks into a composable CI 'stitcher'; introduces a lightweight dependency triage batcher and small dependency bumps; reduces presubmit latency and improves failure signal quality.
description: Context: Our presubmit and release automation logic was fragmented across several GitHub Actions workflows and ad-hoc scripts which made dependency upgrades and release-window coordination error-prone; Motivation: reduce pipeline surface area, lower flakiness, and provide a single place to express staged lint/test profiles and release hooks; What I changed: introduced a CI Stitcher service (declarative manifest + small runner shim) that composes existing workflow fragments at build-time, refactored presubmit profiles into modular manifests, added a dependency refinery job that batches low-risk devdep bumps and produces curated update PRs, upgraded key actions (checkout/setup-node/setup-go) to pinned SHAs, and removed three legacy shell-entrypoints; Tests & validation: local runner smoke tests, staged fastpath on ci/fastlane for 48 hours, integration smoke on release staging, manual dry-run of release hooks; Migration notes: existing workflow filenames are kept for a 2-week deprecation window with no-op redirects to the stitcher; Rollback: revert merge and re-enable old workflows via toggle in ops/ci/config; Risk: moderate during first week for rare tooling edge-cases (toolchain mismatch), mitigations described below.

changed_areas_summary: Composes and replaces multiple fragmented workflow fragments with a declarative stitcher; modularizes presubmit profiles; adds dep triage pipeline; pins action SHAs and cleans legacy scripts; docs and Ops config updates to support a safe rollover.
review_comments: Ethan Zhao: Overall nice consolidation. Question: can we detect action SHA drift automatically in the stitcher?; Asha: Added a follow-up ticket ENG-2107 for auto-checks and included a small validation step in the stitcher that warns on manifest SHA mismatch.

Miguel Santos: The dependency refinery looks powerful but could flood teams with PRs. Suggest rate-limiting and label filtering.; Asha: Added rate-limit config in ops/ci/config.yaml and a label allowlist. Also included a grace period per-repo.

Priya Nair: CI runtime impact? fastlane latency numbers before and after?; Asha: Measured median presubmit latency down from 420s to 310s in fastpath during staged rollout; included metrics export to presubmit latency dashboard and a 'quiet window' toggle.
Ethan Zhao (follow-up): Please add a small e2e that runs the stitcher against a synthetic repo to catch manifest regressions; Asha: Added tools/ci/tests/smoke and CI job for the synthetic repo.
Miguel Santos (approval): Approve after minor docs tweak; Priya Nair: Approve - verified fastlane smoke runs on staging.
ci_checks: integration-smoke: initial run flaky (timeout) -> rerun success
notes_on_rollback_plan: If regressions appear: 1) revert PR; 2) toggle ops/ci/config.yaml to re-enable legacy workflows; 3) re-run presubmit queue with increased telemetry to collect failing manifests. The deprecation scripts will be used to rehydrate the old entrypoints if fast rollback is required.
post_merge_actions: Schedule 1-week post-merge monitoring runbooks, enable presubmit latency dashboard alerts, run dependency-refinery in dry-run mode for 72 hours, and open ENG-2115 to iterate on auto-PR grouping heuristics.
manual_steps_taken_in_merge: Updated Ops config via ops/ci/config.yaml and deployed runner shim to ci-runner-staging; executed scripts/deprecate-old-workflows.sh in dry-run mode to create no-op aliases.
testing_notes: Staged rollout: fastpath enabled for 20% of org repos for 48 hours, then 60% for 24 hours; collected presubmit latency, failure-rate, and flakiness metrics; dependency refinery ran in dry-run for all repos and produced curated PRs for review. No production releases triggered during dry-run.
related_work_items: ENG-2041 (ci consolidation), ENG-2107 (pin verification automation), ENG-2115 (dep-refinery heuristics)
additional_context: This PR is intentionally conservative: it composes pre-existing fragments rather than rewriting them, pins actions to reproducible SHAs, and keeps a short deprecation window for the old workflows to avoid surprise CI disruptions. The dependency refinery's heuristics are intentionally narrow initially (devdeps only, single-package bumps) and will widen after signals are validated.
